title: Spatial omics in cancer: a review of computational approaches and vision of AI-driven analysis.
desc: [Genomics] Predicting patient response to cancer treatments remains a challenge due to tumor heterogeneity and complex tumor microenvironments (TMEs). Modern spatial genomics technologies enable gene expression profiling alongside histological frameworks, but comprehensive analysis and clinical translation of these high-dimensionality datasets will benefit from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). This review synthesizes computational approaches that address challenges of spatial data by examining deep-learning architectures such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for histological feature extraction and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for modeling cell-cell interactions. We then explore the paradigm of Foundation Models that bridge histopathology with transcriptomics to accelerate the identification of spatially resolved biomarkers, improve patient stratification for immunotherapy and targeted treatments, and advance the clinical translation of mechanistic insights derived from the tumor microenvironment.

title: Agent-Driven Generative Priors for Pathology Image Synthesis and Segmentation
desc: Deep learning methods for pathology are constrained by the limited availability and high cost of large-scale pixel-level annotations. Synthetic data can alleviate this limitation, but existing pipelines often lack reliable quality control and remain weakly connected to downstream analysis. To address these issues, we propose a three-stage framework that integrates automated data screening, generative representation learning, and efficient adaptation to downstream tasks. First, we develop a pathology agent system to assess image quality and filter samples, resulting in TCGA-200K, a dataset containing 217,030 pathology patches selected from the public TCGA repository. Second, we train a generative model on the screened data. In addition to image synthesis, its backbone learns structural and semantic representations that can be transferred to downstream tasks. Third, we adapt the pretrained generative backbone to semantic segmentation using a lightweight task-specific head. We further introduce PathSeg-380K, a semantic segmentation dataset with expert annotations for approximately 380,000 cells across 12 cell types. Experiments on multiple pathology datasets show that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art segmentation performance. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/script-Yang/Agent-GenPath.

title: Application of Machine Learning and Deep Learning in diagnosis Covid19
desc: Predicting the progression of COVID-19 in hospitalised patients was an important challenge during the pandemic, particularly when healthcare resources were limited. This study investigates the use of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models to predict three clinical outcomes: death, admission to the intensive care unit (ICU), and clinical status (improvement or worsening). The study uses two patient datasets: an Algerian cohort of 80 patients from the Internal Medicine Department of the University Hospital Centre of Constantine, collected between July and August 2020, and a French cohort of 99 patients collected between March and May 2020. Five ML classifiers were evaluated: logistic regression (LR), k-nearest neighbours (KNN), classification and regression trees (CART), Naive Bayes (NB), and support vector machines (SVM). Their performance was examined in combination with three feature-selection methods: analysis of variance (ANOVA), mutual information (MI), and recursive feature elimination (RFE). The results were also compared with multilayer perceptron (MLP) models using one to five hidden layers. Model evaluation included 30 repetitions of five-fold cross-validation on the training data, followed by evaluation on a separate hold-out test set. The results showed that selecting 20 features generally provided better cross-validated accuracy than selecting 30 features or using the full feature set. The best-performing classifier-feature-selection combination varied across the six dataset-outcome tasks. LR combined with RFE was selected for three tasks, LR combined with ANOVA for one task, and CART combined with ANOVA for two tasks. The selected ML models achieved test-set accuracies ranging from 0.47 to 0.95 and higher accuracy than the average MLP results in five of the six tasks. These findings suggest that ML methods can be useful for exploring clinical outcomes in hospitalised COVID-19 patients. However, the small sample sizes and limitations of the available data mean that the results should be interpreted with caution. Further evaluation using larger and independent patient datasets is needed before these models can be considered for clinical use.

title: Multi-objective domain adaptation for pan-cancer transfer of pharmacogenomic drug response to patient tumours
desc: Large-scale pharmacogenomic screens provide rich drug-sensitivity measurements in cancer cell lines, but transferring these measurements to patient tumours remains limited by biological heterogeneity and cross-domain distribution shift. Existing machine learning approaches, including adversarial autoencoder and domain adaptation, address this gap by learning shared latent representations between preclinical models and patient samples. However, alignment without explicit biological constraints can produce unreliable representations when cancer lineage structure and clinically relevant patient heterogeneity are not preserved. Here, we introduce MODAE+, a pan-cancer multi-objective deep learning domain adaptation framework that jointly balances domain alignment, deconfounding, drug-response prediction, survival prediction, and cancer-lineage classification across 9,696 TCGA tumours, 1,293 CCLE cancer cell lines, and CTRP sensitivity profiles for 544 compounds in 738 matched cell lines. This multi-objective design improved cross-domain alignment while preserving cancer-lineage organization and patient heterogeneity. For drugs shared between the pharmacogenomic screen and TCGA treatment records, MODAE+ predicted sensitivity was significantly associated with overall survival among patients who received each drug in 46.3% of evaluated cancer-drug pairs by log-rank testing and 41.5% by multivariable Cox analysis. Biological validation across four curated drug-gene resources identified significant expression differences exceeding 1.5-fold for 34.9-64.4% of drugs in pan-cancer analyses, based on the lowest-p-value annotated gene per drug. Drug-class-specific patterns involved intended molecular targets for targeted therapies and predominantly transport, metabolism, detoxification and resistance-related genes for classical chemotherapies. As an additional validation, we derived pretreatment responder-nonresponder gene-expression signatures from 13 external breast cancer datasets and evaluated their concordance with MODAE+ predictions across 69 signature-drug comparisons in TCGA patients treated with paclitaxel or doxorubicin. Consensus signature scores showed Spearman correlations of 0.791 with predicted paclitaxel sensitivity and 0.724 with predicted doxorubicin sensitivity, averaging 0.758 across the two drugs. title: Balancing innovation and ethics: responsible governance of artificial intelligence hallucinations in healthcare.
source: PubMed · Philosophy, ethics, and humanities in medicine : PEHM
desc: [Philosophy, ethics, and humanities in medicine : PEHM] Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in healthcare and may improve efficiency in clinical support, health management, and doctor-patient communication. Yet its tendency to hallucinate, that is, to generate medical information that appears plausible but is false, can create systemic ethical risks in high-risk medical settings. This paper addresses two questions: what distinctive ethical risks are created by medical AI hallucinations, and what governance mechanisms can respond to them? Using the four principles of biomedical ethics as an analytical tool, the paper identifies four risk pathways: weakened informed consent, erosion of doctor-patient trust, harm to life and health, and unfair responsibility allocation. It then introduces responsible research and innovation (RRI) to build a four-dimensional framework of anticipation, inclusion, reflexivity, and responsiveness. The main contribution of the paper is to integrate biomedical ethical principles with RRI governance tools in the specific context of medical AI hallucinations, developing a closed-loop governance matrix across technology development, clinical application, and regulatory oversight. This provides an operational pathway for moving medical AI from technical feasibility towards ethical trustworthiness.

title: Trick-or-Treat: Adversarial Evaluation of Multimodal Medical Reasoning with Synthetic Images
desc: We used medical image synthesis to create a challenging multimodal evaluation framework that exposes hallucination behaviors in frontier models. Evaluating multimodal reasoning has historically been difficult because existing medical datasets rarely pair different image modalities, such as radiographs and external clinical photographs. To address this gap, we introduce Trick-or-Treat, an adversarial multimodal medical benchmark that pairs real chest radiographs with synthetic clinical photographs to challenge models' cross-modal reasoning. For each of a wide range of conditions, we created two pairs of images, where the pairs share a single chest radiograph but contain different external photographs. In matched pairs, the chest radiograph and photograph both contain findings suggesting the same disease (e.g., varicella pneumonia suggested by lung opacities and crusted skin lesions seen in chickenpox). In mismatched pairs, the photograph depicts an alternative clinical finding that would not lead to the same unifying diagnosis (e.g. replacing crusted skin lesions with ordinary acne). Synthetic photograph generation allows clinical findings to be varied while the person's features and photographic setting stay consistent, reducing confounding. In an investigation of three frontier models, we found that models hallucinated clinically significant photograph findings in 45-57.5% of mismatched pairs, up from 25-37.5% for the same photographs shown alone. When faced with mismatched pairs, models tended to ignore mismatches and instead hallucinated findings that better matched the radiograph (e.g. misreading acne as crusted skin lesions to justify diagnosing chickenpox). Trick-or-Treat both demonstrates concerning error pattern in frontier models' medical reasoning and provides a proof of concept for the use of synthetic images in adversarial multimodal evaluation.

title: First-trimester nocturnal cardiorespiratory coupling during home sleep testing and later pregnancy complications: a secondary analysis of the nuMoM2b cohort
desc: We tested whether direction-specific nocturnal cardiorespiratory coupling (CRC) in the first trimester differed in pregnancies that later developed obstetric complications. The analysis included 2504 nulliparous women from the nuMoM2b cohort with valid level 3 home sleep recordings at 6-13 weeks' gestation. Bidirectional CRC between RR intervals and abdominal respiratory effort was quantified using bivariate phase-rectified signal averaging in consecutive 5-min segments. Coupling strength, local transition dynamics, and waveform irregularity were summarized by nightly mean and standard deviation. Associations with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM; n = 111), preeclampsia (n = 149), preterm birth (n = 192), and fetal macrosomia (n = 186) were examined using proportional-odds models with CRC feature quintile as the ordered outcome. Models included all four complications simultaneously and adjusted for maternal age, pre-pregnancy body mass index, race and ethnicity, gestational age at recording, relevant medical and family history, medication use, and apnea-hypopnea index >5 events/h. Holm correction was applied across outcomes. GDM was associated with lower respiration-to-heart rate coupling strength (cumulative odds ratio, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.31-0.64; P < 0.001) and shallower slope at the anchor point (0.63; 0.45-0.89; P = 0.03). Fetal macrosomia was associated with lower within-night variability in heart rate-to-respiration waveform irregularity (0.59; 0.45-0.77; P < 0.001). No associations with preeclampsia or preterm birth remained significant after correction. Direction-specific differences in nocturnal CRC were detectable in the first trimester in pregnancies that later developed GDM or resulted in fetal macrosomia.

title: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction
desc: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder. PALM was trained on ~15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17,951 domain and 1,383 site classes. Across 2.3 million held-out proteins, PALM achieved domain- and site-occurrence F1 scores of 0.941 and 0.877, respectively, and retained substantial performance in proteins with <20% sequence identity to the training and validation data. PALM also substantially outperformed ESM3 annotation baseline. Without training on variant-pathogenicity labels, PALM embedding disruption distinguished 151,823 ClinVar missense variants more accurately than ESM2 embedding disruption (AUROC 0.835 versus 0.710), and combining PALM embedding disruption with the ESM2 likelihood-ratio signal reached an AUROC of 0.877. The same combined zero-shot score outperformed AlphaMissense on a benchmark dataset on 128,161 missense variants, that were derived from literature but not present in ClinVar database. At the protein level, PALM embeddings showed stronger CATH-Gene3D superfamily organization than frozen ESM2 and ESM3 embeddings, and improved prediction of experimental activation and repression effects when combined with ESM2. In a downstream case study, we demonstrated the ability to use PALM-derived embedding as proxy of deep mutational scanning (DMS), showcasing the broad application of PALM. Together, PALM converts curated residue-level knowledge into transferable and mechanistically interpretable representations that connect protein sequence, function, and variant consequence.

title: Mathematical foundations of artificial intelligence in healthcare: a systematic review.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare relies on diverse mathematical frameworks, yet their contributions to model development, evaluation, interpretability, and clinical translation remain fragmented. This systematic review synthesized the classical and emerging mathematical foundations underpinning healthcare AI and examined major methodological and application trends. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, studies published between January 2016 and June 30, 2026, were identified through systematic searches of Scopus, Google Scholar, and PubMed/MEDLINE, with searches conducted using Harzing's Publish or Perish v8 where applicable. Bibliometric analysis was performed using VOSviewer, while methodological quality was assessed using an adapted JBI-based framework and AMSTAR-2 for systematic reviews. Of 653 records identified, 147 studies met the eligibility criteria. Non-mutually exclusive mathematical-domain coding identified linear algebra in 100/147 studies (68.0%), calculus and optimization in 91/147 (61.9%), and probability and statistics in 79/147 (53.7%), highlighting their roles in data representation, learning, optimization, inference, uncertainty quantification, and validation. A separate mutually exclusive classification of dominant methodological themes identified explainable and trustworthy AI in 24/147 studies (16.3%), statistics and learning theory in 23/147 (15.6%), probability and Bayesian methods in 23/147 (15.6%), calculus and optimization in 19/147 (12.9%), and linear algebra in 15/147 (10.2%). Radiology and medical imaging were the leading healthcare application (24.3%), while classification and diagnosis were the most frequent clinical task (17.1%). Overall, healthcare AI is supported by an interconnected mathematical ecosystem. Emerging approaches, including graph neural networks, Transformers, and quantum machine learning, require stronger external validation, standardized benchmarking, and rigorous evaluation for reliable clinical translation.

title: A Frame-Level View and Image-Quality Annotation Tool for Fetal Echocardiography: Comparison with Spreadsheet Annotation
desc: Objective: To develop the Cardiologist Annotation Tool (CAT) for frame-level cardiac view and image-quality annotation in fetal echocardiography and compare it with spreadsheet-based annotation. Methods: CAT provides cine playback, frame navigation, and keyboard-based labeling without manual frame-range entry. Experts annotated 25 studies using both methods, and spreadsheet annotations were audited for predefined data-entry errors. In a randomized crossover study, six medical students annotated two normal studies, one with each method, against an expert reference. Results: Among 1,746 spreadsheet-annotated files, 6.2% contained major or critical data-entry errors, more frequently in congenital heart disease than normal studies (10.9% vs 3.4%). CAT yielded more annotated view segments per clip (3.6 vs 1.5). Rates of labeled and correctly labeled frames per minute were 1.77 and 1.68 times those with spreadsheets, respectively (both P = 0.031), with gains in all six students. No detectable difference in view-label accuracy was observed. Conclusion: CAT eliminates manual frame-range entry and enables finer-grained, structured annotation of fetal echocardiography, providing a practical approach to preparing datasets for AI research.

title: FeatureMAP enables network-guided interpretation of untargeted metabolomics
desc: Untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) metabolomics generates thousands of features, but incomplete metabolite annotation and reliance on predefined pathways limit their biological interpretation. Here we present FeatureMAP, an LC-MS feature-centric computational framework that integrates multi-evidence metabolite annotation, network-guided refinement, metabolic module discovery, and structured large language model-based functional interpretation. Across ten public datasets, FeatureMAP improved MS1-based metabolite candidate prioritization while reducing annotation redundancy. In semi-synthetic benchmarks, FeatureMAP recovered coordinated metabolic perturbations, achieving 92% recovery of a simulated perturbation, and distinguished concurrent metabolic processes. Controlled benchmarks further evaluated functional interpretation under competing metabolite-level signals. Based on FeatureMAP, we additionally developed PhenoMAP, a phenotype-aware knowledge graph comprising 12,929 dysregulated metabolic modules from 501 human metabolomics studies spanning 326 phenotypes. Module-level comparisons revealed reproducible metabolic similarities across independent studies and biologically supported relationships among phenotypes. Application to Alzheimer's disease cerebrospinal fluid and cellular datasets identified convergent membrane-lipid alterations and implicated galactose-linked glycosphingolipid remodeling. Together, FeatureMAP and PhenoMAP enable network-grounded interpretation of incompletely annotated LC-MS metabolomics data and systematic investigation of metabolic dysregulation across biological conditions.

title: Applying artificial intelligence to optical coherence tomography for detection and subtyping of basal cell carcinoma.
source: PubMed · Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft = Journal of the German Society of Dermatology : JDDG
desc: [Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft = Journal of the German Society of Dermatology : JDDG] Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common cancer and a major public health burden. Noninvasive techniques such as optical coherence tomography (OCT) may reduce unnecessary biopsies and enable earlier detection. However, effective OCT interpretation requires expertise. Artificial intelligence (AI) may help overcome this barrier. An AI model based on a U-Net convolutional neural network was trained using 4,680 annotated OCT image frames from 39 BCCs, 5,640 frames from 47 premalignant and benign lesions, and 12,360 frames from 103 scans of healthy skin. Detection performance was evaluated on an independent test set comprising 26 scans (3,120 frames) from 16 BCCs, 5 premalignant lesions, and 5 benign lesions. External validation used independent clinical data from 25 histologically confirmed BCCs (18 nodular, 7 superficial). AI-assisted OCT generated visual overlays corresponding to established BCC features and identified tumor areas. In the independent test set, the area under the ROC curve was 95.5 % for nodular and 98.2 % for superficial BCC. In clinical validation, all BCCs were detected, and subtype concordance with histology was achieved in 21 of 25 cases (83 %). AI-assisted OCT shows potential to improve non-invasive BCC diagnostics and warrants further clinical evaluation.

title: From Vision to Context: A Review of Prompt-Driven Target Volume Segmentation in Radiotherapy
desc: Accurate target volume (TV) segmentation is essential for radiotherapy (RT) planning but remains time-consuming. Moreover, the final contour depends on the expertise of the radiation oncologist. Although deep learning has improved medical image segmentation, image-only models cannot encode the clinical reasoning that governs TV delineation, particularly for the clinical target volume (CTV), where boundaries are defined by clinical knowledge rather than imaging features alone. Prompt-driven segmentation has recently emerged as a strategy to address this limitation. This work aims to review these approaches for RT TV segmentation with four objectives: (1) compare the different prompting techniques used; (2) compare their performance against image-only baselines; (3) assess how they are evaluated against standard metrics, including the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th Hausdorff distance, sensitivity, precision, and clinical assessment; and (4) identify the gaps needed for clinical translation. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and arXiv for studies incorporating geometric, clinical text, or interactive prompts into deep learning models for RT TV delineation. Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria, spanning head and neck, breast, prostate, lung, cervix, and rectal cancers. Seven studies used clinical text prompting, four used geometric prompting, and two used interactive prompting; three combined modalities. Reported DSC ranged from 0.67 to 0.93, compared to 0.65 to 0.91 for image-only baselines. None reported sensitivity or precision. Clinical text prompting appears well suited to CTV delineation. Evidence remains limited, and standardized prompt engineering and clinical validation are needed before these approaches can be translated into routine RT practice.

title: Harnessing catalytic knowledge to guide enzyme discovery and evolution with AlphaEnzyme
desc: Retrieving an enzyme for a target reaction provides a starting point for evolution, but predicting how to improve it remains difficult. This requires connecting evolutionary information with the structural and chemical context of catalysis. Here we present AlphaEnzyme, an enzyme foundation model built on a structure-grounded representation of an enzyme paired with its reaction, from which catalytic compatibility, kinetics and mutational response are read out together. On a time-separated benchmark, AlphaEnzyme achieves a top-1 catalyst retrieval success rate of 30.1%, against 17.2% for the strongest baseline. Michaelis constant predictions achieve the highest rank correlations among the compared methods, reaching 0.64 for enzymes sharing at most 40% identity with the kinetic training set. The model also enriches high-fitness TrpB variants at a budget of 16 candidates without target-specific fitness training. In prospective transaminase engineering, several prioritized variants exceed the parent, with the best design yielding a 30.4-fold increase in product signal in a lysate-based assay while retaining (R)-selectivity. Together, AlphaEnzyme provides a common molecular basis for selecting starting enzymes and prioritizing sequence changes for their improvement.

Artificial Intelligence in Uveitis: Where Are We on the Translational Pathway?
desc: [Clinical & experimental ophthalmology] Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed several areas of ophthalmic practice, most notably diabetic retinopathy screening, where autonomous systems have achieved regulatory approval and real-world deployment. Uveitis, by contrast, remains at an earlier stage in translation. Its heterogeneity, longitudinal disease course and reliance on multimodal clinical reasoning present distinct challenges, compounded by small, fragmented and geographically restricted datasets. This review examines the landscape of AI applications in uveitis and maps them to the established ophthalmic AI validation pipeline, from algorithm development through to clinical deployment. Evidence varies between individual studies: selected vitritis detection and aetiological classification models have undergone independent external testing, while anterior chamber inflammation quantification includes small single-centre feasibility studies. Emerging applications, including recurrent-course prediction, treatment-response modelling, fluorescein angiography segmentation, natural language processing and foundation model fine-tuning, remain predominantly at proof-of-concept stages. Despite encouraging algorithmic performance, the studies discussed have not demonstrated clinical actionability: evidence that an AI output changes a clinical decision, leads to an appropriate management intervention and ultimately improves a patient-relevant outcome. We argue that the principal translational bottleneck is therefore not algorithmic capability alone, but the absence of harmonised longitudinal datasets, geographically diverse validation, prospective evaluation and, critically, studies linking AI output → clinical decision → management intervention → patient outcome. International collaborative registries offer a pathway towards addressing these gaps. The next phase of uveitis AI must move beyond model performance towards clinically actionable systems that improve diagnosis, disease monitoring, treatment selection and relapse prediction, ultimately delivering meaningful benefit to patients with ocular inflammatory disease.

title: Spatially and Compositionally Controlled Multimodal Glioblastoma MRI Synthesis with Latent Diffusion
desc: Glioblastoma exhibits substantial heterogeneity in tumour morphology and composition across MRI modalities, often making available clinical datasets highly unbalanced in terms of patient pathologies. We propose a two-stage latent diffusion model (LDM) framework for the generation of explicitly controllable 2D glioblastoma MRI scans. First, a segmentation LDM generates tumour maps conditioned on location, spatial extent, axial position, and subregion composition. Second, a modality-conditioned LDM with ControlNet generates T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR images adhering to the requested segmentation. On a held-out test set, generated segmentations achieved a mean centroid error of 0.842 pixels and a subregion proportion error of 0.795 percentage points. ControlNet improved Fréchet inception distance (FID) across all four modalities, reducing pooled FID from 42.59 to 36.12. An expert reader study yielded mean quality ratings of 6.60 for real images, 6.83 for ControlNet-generated images, and 6.77 for fully synthetic images.

title: A review of medical image segmentation research based on bibliometrics.
source: PubMed · Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
desc: [Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine] BackgroundMedical image segmentation is a fundamental step in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning, and its research landscape has expanded rapidly with the advancement of artificial intelligence. A systematic bibliometric overview of this field is therefore needed to clarify its intellectual structure and emerging trends.ObjectiveTo provide a comprehensive bibliometric overview of the global research landscape, developmental trends, collaboration networks, and emerging hotspots in the field of medical image segmentation over the past decade.MethodsA bibliometric analysis was performed on 21,437 publications related to medical image segmentation, indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2016 to 2025. The analysis systematically examined publication outputs, country-level contributions, author collaboration networks, journal distributions, and keyword co-occurrence patterns.ResultsThe annual publication count increased remarkably from 25 in 2016 to 5,207 in 2025. China contributed the largest share with 11,556 publications, followed by the United States (3,272) and India (1,924). Core researchers formed stable intra-team collaborations, though inter-team cooperation remained limited. Keyword and citation analyses identified deep learning, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Transformers, U-Net, and their variants as dominant methodological themes. Case studies on skin and lung segmentation revealed differential research attention and international collaboration patterns across anatomical targets. A historical trajectory analysis showed methodological evolution from traditional image processing to fully convolutional networks and U-Net, and subsequently to hybrid architectures integrating attention mechanisms and Transformers.ConclusionMedical image segmentation has experienced substantial growth, driven by deep learning innovations. Future research may increasingly focus on multimodal foundation models capable of generalizable segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios. This bibliometric review offers researchers a valuable reference for understanding the intellectual structure and frontiers of the field.

title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
desc: Researchers use large language models as agents in social simulations, where agents are prompted with observations and background information intended to shape their actions. Yet LLM agents have been shown to substantially change their behavior under meaning-preserving prompt variations, creating a validation problem for social simulation. One plausible hypothesis is that this brittleness reflects a lack of grounding and can be reduced by enriching the context provided to the agents. Whether richer context improves robustness remains unclear, in part because context richness and robustness are rarely defined in ways that support controlled comparisons. We address the first need with controlled context enrichment, a set of prompt substitution rules that systematically enriches distinct types of context: neutral padding, generic social background, descriptive decision grounding, and normative decision grounding. We address the second by introducing selective robustness as a validation criterion: insensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt variation combined with a directional response to decision-relevant changes in the social world. We demonstrate the framework in a Prisoner's Dilemma-like game, showing how it can be used to identify which forms of context enrichment produce more desirable and robust agent behavior. We find that these forms of enrichment produce distinct behavioral patterns that vary between the two models tested.

title: Exosomes in regenerative medicine from biological messengers to engineered nanocarriers for precision therapeutics.
desc: [Discover nano] Exosomes have emerged as a promising class of next-generation nanocarriers at the intersection of regenerative medicine and drug delivery. Compared with conventional synthetic nanocarriers and stem cell-based therapies, exosomes offer unique advantages, including intrinsic biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, blood-barrier penetration, and natural intercellular cargo transfer. This review critically examines exosome biology, beginning with their biogenesis, structural composition, and roles in cellular homeostasis, immune regulation, autophagy, and tissue repair. Particular emphasis is placed on their therapeutic relevance in wound healing, neuroregeneration, cardiovascular repair, musculoskeletal regeneration, and cancer. The review further discusses major strategies for exosomal cargo engineering, including passive loading, electroporation, sonication, transfection-based approaches, extrusion, freeze-thaw treatment, and chemical functionalization. In addition, scaffold-assisted delivery systems and hybrid exosome-synthetic nanocarrier platforms are highlighted as important advances for improving local retention, targeting precision, and controlled release. Despite strong preclinical promise, translation remains limited by challenges in scalable manufacturing, purification, batch consistency, loading efficiency, potency assessment, and regulatory standardization. Future progress in this field will depend on the development of scalable and GMP-compatible exosome manufacturing, standardized purification and characterization methods, validated potency assays, regulatory-aligned quality control, and artificial intelligence (AI) engineering strategies to translate exosome-based platforms into safe, reproducible, and clinically effective regenerative therapeutics.

title: PINR-ESI: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Implicit Neural Representation Framework for EEG Extended-Source Imaging
desc: EEG extended-source imaging aims to localize active cortical regions and characterize their spatial extent, yet supervised inverse networks typically depend on synthetic EEG-source pairs and may be sensitive to synthetic-to-real mismatch. We propose a physics-informed self-supervised implicit neural representation (INR) framework for spatial source reconstruction without paired source labels or simulation-based supervised pretraining. The lead field matrix encodes the source-to-sensor volume-conduction model and constrains the INR through agreement between predicted and measured EEG. Cortical current density is modeled as a continuous coordinate-conditioned field. A classical inverse estimate provides warm initialization and spatial constraints on source activity, while patch-integrated projection maps the field to discrete source coefficients for forward modeling. Simulations with varying noise levels, source counts, and source extents showed the clearest advantage in identifying active cortical regions, particularly for multiple and larger sources. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations using real EEG recordings from epilepsy patients and intracranial stimulation experiments further supported the feasibility of the framework for source imaging. These findings suggest the potential of physics-informed self-supervised INR for extended-source imaging.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Cardiovascular Health Behavior Change: A Narrative Review of Patient-Facing Tools.
source: PubMed · Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education
desc: [Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education] Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States and disproportionately affects racial/ethnic minoritized populations, low-income communities, older adults, and rural residents. Behavioral interventions can reduce cardiovascular risk, yet traditional programs face scalability barriers, including high costs and limited reach. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the efficacy and equity of patient-directed AI tools that support health education and behavior change for cardiovascular health. Using PRISMA-ScR elements, we searched 10 databases (January 2010 to December 2025), yielding 19 empirical studies evaluating Generation 2.0 AI systems aligned with the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework. Of these, five were randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and 14 were nonrandomized (quasi-experimental, observational, or early-stage) studies. AI-enabled interventions such as conversational agents, machine-learning models, and reinforcement-learning systems addressed hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, and related conditions. Among the RCTs, one demonstrated superiority of an AI-powered program over usual care (AI-delivered Diabetes Prevention Program), whereas the remaining four reported outcomes equivalent or non-inferior to standard behavioral care. Effects were most apparent in high-intensity interventions that paired machine learning-based personalization with structured behavioral curricula, although the multi-component nature of these programs limits inference about AI-specific contributions. Across nonrandomized studies, greater engagement intensity was consistently associated with improved cardiometabolic outcomes, although causal attribution to AI-specific mechanisms remains limited. Most studies had small samples, short follow-up, and limited reporting on safety and equity. Technology-intensive interventions were concentrated in higher-resourced settings, and populations with limited health literacy showed reduced engagement. Overall, evidence supports cautious optimism that AI can meaningfully scale personalized cardiovascular prevention; however, realizing that equitable and clinically meaningful impact will require rigorous trials with longer follow-up, explicit behavioral science integration, safety-conscious governance, and equity-centered strategies addressing digital determinants of health.

title: LungMend: A Healthy-Only Latent Diffusion Shape Prior for Lung Mask Correction in Severe Tuberculosis CT
desc: Lung segmentation models such as R231 are widely used, but they fail on severe tuberculosis (TB) CT: cavities and consolidations look like non-lung tissue and are left out of the mask. We present LungMend, a post-processing model that corrects such masks using only healthy anatomy. A latent diffusion model, trained on healthy lungs with synthetically corrupted masks, learns to recover the complete lung from the faulty mask and the bone anatomy, without any pathological data or CT intensities. LungMend recovers cavities and consolidations that R231 misses and improves accuracy on expert-annotated slices. Code: https://github.com/noureddinekhiati/LungMend

title: Green AI for Telehealth.
desc: [Healthcare management forum] Telehealth is increasingly supported by connected devices, remote monitoring, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and distributed computing. These tools can extend access and support more responsive care, but their computational and environmental demands are rarely considered alongside clinical and organizational needs. We describe the current Canadian telehealth landscape, including remote care management, virtual visits, patient portals, and remote monitoring, and identify opportunities and gaps for AI integration. We then define Green AI in healthcare and explain how an IoT-fog-cloud architecture can support resource-aware telehealth. For health leaders, Green AI is not only an engineering issue. It affects procurement, infrastructure planning, workforce capacity, clinical workflow, environmental responsibility, and equity. Evaluation should consider clinical performance, resource use, organizational fit, and sustainability. Responsible AI-enabled telehealth requires more than technical performance. A Green AI perspective can help health organizations improve computational efficiency while maintaining patient safety, usable workflows, resilience, and equitable access.

title: Vibrational spectroscopy and artificial intelligence for dynamic phenotypic characterization of antimicrobial resistance.
source: PubMed · Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
desc: [Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology] The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance has created an urgent need for diagnostic technologies capable of rapidly identifying resistant phenotypes and informing precision antimicrobial therapy. Conventional antimicrobial susceptibility testing methods remain clinically reliable; however, they are limited by relatively long turnaround times and restricted physiological resolution. In recent years, vibrational spectroscopy techniques have emerged as promising platforms for rapid phenotypic microbiology because they generate label-free biochemical fingerprints associated with proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and membrane biomolecules. When integrated with machine learning and artificial intelligence, these technologies could provide highly sensitive tools for rapid bacterial classification, resistance prediction, and monitoring of dynamic physiological adaptation during antibiotic exposure. This review discusses the integration of chemometrics, machine learning, and deep learning algorithms with spectroscopic datasets, emphasizing both predictive performance and biological interpretability. It is highly useful for bacterial identification, biochemical characterization, and resistance profiling across multiple microbial species. Major controversies regarding genotype-versus-phenotype diagnostics, reproducibility, standardization, and AI explainability are also examined. Finally, we highlight current research gaps and future directions, including single-cell spectroscopy, multimodal phenotyping, explainable AI frameworks, and approaches in systems microbiology. Taken together, the available evidence indicates that integrating vibrational spectroscopy with artificial intelligence could substantially reshape future antimicrobial resistance diagnostics and mechanistic microbiology.

title: Deep Learning for AD Risk Screening and Progression Prediction.
desc: [Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany)] The rise of Alzheimer's disease (AD) immunotherapies underscores the need for accessible, time-efficient biomarkers for early diagnosis. MRI-based deep learning shows promise in this regard, yet few models have undergone comprehensive clinical validation. Using the SILCODE cohort (722 Chinese participants, 1,105 scans), we test the transportability of our classifier (pretrained on Western samples) to an independent Chinese cohort without retraining. The associations between risk scores and disease progression, cognitive performance, and plasma biomarkers are examined. In addition, an interpretable framework is developed to generate individualized brain risk maps and identify subtypes. The model classifies AD with an AUC of 0.913 and 95.2% sensitivity, identifying 90.5% of high-risk individuals 2-3 years before clinical diagnosis. Risk scores correlate significantly with cognitive and plasma indices, particularly p-tau 217. Brain risk maps reveal AD subtypes, including a subgroup with rapid cognitive decline. These findings establish a population-robust, clinically relevant MRI-based model for early AD detection and risk stratification.

title: AI Identifies Clinically Relevant Asystole Among False Loop Recorder Alerts: From Data Overload to Diagnosis.
desc: [JACC. Case reports] Implantable loop recorders (ILRs) are often implanted to investigate unexplained syncopal episodes. However, ILRs may produce false alerts due to undersensing or artifacts, thus requiring careful review of numerous device recordings, which makes it challenging to identify clinically significant events. We report a case of a 77-year-old woman with recurrent syncopal episodes, in whom a 7-second pause was detected by an ILR. Device interrogations showed multiple pause alerts that were identified as false events because of poor R sensing. However, the artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced remote monitoring identified a true pause with blocked P waves, leading the patient to receive a pacemaker implantation. This case highlights the clinical value of AI-assisted remote monitoring in identifying clinically relevant arrhythmias among numerous device alerts. Improved automated filtering of ILR data may reduce diagnostic delays and help clinicians prioritize clinically significant events. ILRs may generate numerous false alerts because of sensing abnormalities, complicating the identification of clinically relevant events in routine practice. AI-enhanced remote monitoring may improve diagnostic efficiency by identifying true arrhythmic events within large volumes of device-generated data and guiding timely management.

title: Contextual Semantic Pattern Recognition for Mental Health Monitoring Using ClinicalBERT Transformers.
desc: [Brain and behavior] This study aimed to develop an interpretable ClinicalBERT-based framework for mental health monitoring using structured clinical data. Because the Mental Health Diagnosis and Treatment Monitoring dataset contains structured patient attributes rather than free-text clinical narratives, a structured-to-text transformation module was used to convert the records into contextual descriptions suitable for ClinicalBERT. The proposed model was compared with Random Forest, XGBoost, Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), TabTransformer, and a Deep Neural Network, and to strengthen the experimental comparison, contemporary tabular transformer models, including SAINT and FT-Transformer, were also evaluated. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Cross-validation, confidence interval analysis, statistical significance testing, and ablation experiments were conducted to examine the reliability of the results. SHAP and LIME were used to explain global feature contributions and individual predictions. ClinicalBERT achieved an accuracy of 90.2%, a precision of 90.5%, a recall of 90.4%, and an F1-score of 90.6%, outperforming all comparison models. The additional validation analyses supported the stability of the results. SHAP and LIME further identified the patient attributes that contributed most strongly to the model's predictions. The findings indicate that structured clinical records can be transformed into contextual representations for transformer-based mental health monitoring. The framework combines predictive performance with interpretable output, although its evaluation is currently limited to a single dataset. Further validation using multi-institutional and prospective data is required.

title: AI in health care: from clinical support to algorithmic management?
desc: [Health policy (Amsterdam, Netherlands)] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in health care to improve the quality of care, support clinical decision-making, and increase efficiency. As AI systems are integrated into healthcare workflows, they can also become involved in how work is managed, including directing tasks, coordinating workflows, monitoring activity, and evaluating performance. These managerial uses of digital and AI systems are commonly referred to as forms of algorithmic management. Such uses may contribute to the intended benefits of AI, but may also make work more standardised, measurable, and monitorable, potentially increasing managerial control, reducing professional autonomy, or intensifying work. Whether these consequences arise depends on how these systems are implemented and governed. Realising AI's potential in health care therefore requires explicit choices about how AI is used within healthcare organisations and how gains from automation are allocated, so that benefits for care are maximised while potential harms are limited.

title: Extracellular Vesicles in Soft Tissue Sarcomas: from Tumor Biology to Clinical Translation.
desc: [Critical reviews in oncology/hematology] Soft tissue sarcomas (STS) comprise a rare, highly heterogeneous group of mesenchymal malignancies characterized by diverse molecular drivers, poor prognosis, and a lack of biomarkers for disease monitoring and therapeutic stratification. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as key mediators of intercellular communication and promising tools in precision oncology. By transporting cargoes, including oncogenic signals reflecting the molecular state of their cells of origin, EVs influence tumor progression, immune modulation, angiogenesis and metastatic dissemination. In line with MISEV2023 standards and advances in clinical translation, this review provides a timely, histotype-stratified synthesis of EV biology in STS, integrating EV-based biomarker discovery with engineered delivery platforms and the regulatory challenges of rare-disease translation. We examine EV biology across STS subtypes, including liposarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, fibrosarcoma, and leiomyosarcoma, highlighting how subtype-specific EV-cargo reprograms the tumor microenvironment. Moving from bench to bedside, we discuss the translational potential of EVs as minimally invasive liquid biopsy tools. Rather than replacing existing circulating markers, EVs may provide orthogonal diagnostic and tumor microenvironment remodeling signals that complement ctDNA, supporting a histotype-dependent approach for longitudinal monitoring and minimal residual disease (MRD) detection. Finally, we critically address the technical and regulatory challenges to clinical implementation, including isolation heterogeneity, Good Manufacturing Practice scalability, and quality control. To overcome these hurdles, we propose a translational roadmap encompassing integrated biobanking networks, multicenter clinical validation, and artificial intelligence-driven analytical platforms. Overall, EVs represent a promising but still investigational platform, offering unprecedented opportunities for patient stratification, disease surveillance, and personalized therapeutic strategies in aggressive sarcomas.

title: [From personalized medicine to new approaches for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma].
desc: [La Revue du praticien] Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is one of the most aggressive cancers, partly due to its high degree of heterogeneity. While common mutations such as KRAS or TP53 are well known, they offered, until recently, few direct therapeutic targets. In contrast, some rare alterations such as germline BRCA mutations or mismatch repair deficiency (MMR) open the door to targeted therapies or immunotherapy. Advances in molecular biology have led to the identification of transcriptomic subtypes, such as the "classical" and "basal-like", each associated with different prognoses. These subtypes are now complemented by predictive transcriptomic signatures, assisted by artificial intelligence, which may help guide chemotherapy choices after prospective validation. Innovative approaches, including neoantigen-based vaccines and RAS inhibitors, have shown promising results. At the same time, the development of experimental models like organoids and xenografts allows for preclinical testing of therapies. Ultimately, given the complexity of the disease, personalized treatment strategies are now being combined with broader approaches to reach a larger population of patients.

title: Hallucinations in generative LLMs for radiology: a comprehensive review.
source: PubMed · Current problems in diagnostic radiology
desc: [Current problems in diagnostic radiology] Hallucinations generated by large language models (LLMs) represent an emerging safety top event in radiology, where subtle interpretive errors can rapidly propagate into clinical decisions. Although these systems demonstrate remarkable linguistic fluency, their underlying probabilistic architecture is, in some cases, not aligned with the demands of diagnostic intelligence, factual reliability, or safety standards. This work presents a comprehensive review describing the pathways that lead to hallucinations in radiology domain generative LLMs, mapping the risks derived from model architecture, data quality, black-box opacity, and automation bias. It also identifies the preventive strategies required to control these risks, including legal and governance safeguards, rigorous data curation protocols, explainability and simulation frameworks, and structured human oversight. This review shows how hallucinations may distort diagnostic reasoning, generate fictitious clinical data, and precipitate erroneous management decisions with potential patient harm, underscoring the need for controlled deployment strategies before integrating generative AI into radiological workflows.

title: Wearable Arrhythmia Detection: Moving from your Watch to your Shirt?
desc: [Current cardiology reports] Digital devices play an increasingly important role in the detection and screening of cardiac arrhythmias. Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common arrhythmia, is associated with an increased risk of stroke, heart failure, and mortality. This review summarises the current evidence on wearable devices for screening and diagnosing atrial fibrillation. Numerous studies have demonstrated the value of wearables for AF detection and diagnosis. In addition, artificial intelligence enhances automated rhythm analysis and signal processing, supporting the increasing clinical implementation of digital technologies in outpatient care. Single-lead ECG devices provide the strongest evidence for AF detection, with smartwatches representing one of the most extensively investigated wearable technology. Limitations include motion artefacts and predominantly semi-continuous monitoring. Future research should focus on integrating artificial intelligence to improve signal analysis and artefact reduction, and on evaluating the impact of wearable-based strategies on clinically relevant outcomes, including stroke and heart failure.

title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity.
desc: [Nature] Cancer cells show highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour1-5. However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here we generated a deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across many regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalizes tumours into distinct tissue microenvironments and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Consistently, using a new deep-learning framework to map cancer cell states jointly with clones in situ, we show that tumour subclones are finely spatially intermixed through glioblastoma tissue microenvironments. We validate this cellular trajectory by using somatic mutation-based hierarchies in vivo and an experimental patient-derived organoid model ex vivo. Finally, we show that this cancer cell trajectory is intimately linked to myeloid heterogeneity and unfolds across regionalized myeloid signalling environments. Our findings define a stereotyped trajectory of cancer cells in glioblastoma and unify glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity into a tractable cellular and tissue framework.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Brain Arteriovenous Malformation Neuroimaging: A Scoping Review of Clinical Applications, Performance, and Translation Readiness.
source: PubMed · Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie
desc: [Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie] Artificial intelligence (AI) is used in brain arteriovenous malformation (AVM) neuroimaging, but translation readiness remains incompletely mapped. To characterize AI-related applications, reported performance, and barriers to clinical deployment. We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided review of PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar from inception through 20 December 2025, with PubMed additionally searched on 23 August 2026. Eligible sources addressed AI, machine learning, radiomics, or automated computational analysis of brain AVM imaging. Results were charted descriptively; heterogeneous metrics were not pooled. Thirty-two sources were included: 28 primary reports and four contextual evidence syntheses. Thirteen primary reports had a documented AI/ML component. Of these, seven used imaging-derived inputs only, three combined imaging with clinical or treatment predictors, one compared separate imaging and clinical models, and two had unresolved final predictor sets. Three nidus-segmentation reports gave Dice estimates of 0.754, 0.80 and 0.82; partition details were unavailable for the first, and the last applied to detected lesions. Validation designs and clinical targets varied, precluding a pooled performance estimate. AI/ML shows technical feasibility in selected brain AVM imaging and prediction tasks. Clinical benefit and routine deployment have not been demonstrated. Multicenter institutional validation, calibration, transparent reporting and prospective clinical-impact evaluation remain priorities.

title: A retrieval-augmented multi-stage prompting framework for legal analysis in the Indian judicial system.
desc: [Frontiers in big data] The aim of this endeavor was to create an Artificial Intelligence (AI) based legal researcher that utilizes a multi-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methodology to solve the challenges of finding and comprehending pertinent legal information in the documents. The traditional methods for finding legal documents will usually yield very few results that are useful to someone without a law degree. This new system uses semantic search, keyword retrieval and Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning methods to improve the legal research process. The submitted query will be transformed into a vector embedding while simultaneously being classified into the appropriate category for retrieval. Once the query is classified, the system will use a hybrid retrieval mechanism to find the most relevant legal document based on both BM25 (Best Matching 25) and FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) search algorithms and will combine these results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) in order to determine the best results. Later, it will be processed through LLM models to produce formatted (structured) answers to the query in accordance with the relevant legal citation. The overall performance of the proposed system demonstrates improved answer relevancy, reliability and contextual accuracy, thereby making it an effective tool for legal research and assistance. LLaMA-3.3-70B achieved the highest scores in Answer Relevancy (0.91) and Faithfulness (0.92), proving its ability to generate accurate, intent aligned, and evidence-grounded legal responses with minimal hallucination. Gemini-2.0-Flash showed higher Context Recall (0.78), indicating strong retrieval capability, while Mistral-Large excelled in BLEU (0.769) and semantic similarity, highlighting fluent text generation but weaker evidence grounding.

title: Therapeutic Functions in Large Language Model Responses to Emotional Disclosures: Qualitative Content Analysis.
desc: [JMIR formative research] Millions of people now use general-purpose large language models (LLMs) for mental health support, yet how these models respond to emotional disclosures and whether their responses functionally resemble established therapeutic practices remain uncharacterized. This study aimed to characterize how frontier LLMs respond to emotionally charged messages and examine whether their response patterns resemble therapeutic practices associated with self-awareness. We generated 54 simulated user inputs representing mild-to-moderate everyday emotional difficulties. These simulated user inputs were generated using 3 LLMs (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, and Gemini 2.5 Pro). The simulated user inputs systematically varied across 3 lengths and 5 communicative registers, ranging from raw venting to pragmatic requests. Then, each simulated user input was presented as a standalone user turn to the same 3 frontier LLMs, yielding 162 responses. Two independent clinical coders qualitatively coded the resulting responses using an inductive approach. The codes were compared and consolidated through iterative consensus, which yielded 8 higher-order categories. Acknowledging and validating segments appeared in 89.5% (145/162) of responses, emotion-focused suggestions in 84.6% (137/162), and interpretation in 67.3% (109/162). These patterns converged on emotional self-awareness, a construct associated with adaptive emotion regulation, suggesting that LLMs may repeatedly enact a recognizable micro-process of validation, affect labeling, interpretation, reflection, and regulation support. Models differed in stance, with some assigning emotional labels and interpretations directly rather than prompting users' own reflection. Frontier LLMs respond to emotional disclosures in patterned, largely convergent ways that approximate therapeutic techniques for building emotional awareness, though delivered more didactically than in clinical practice. Whether these responses build genuine self-awareness, reduce symptoms, or provide therapeutic benefit requires controlled and naturalistic investigation.

title: Can large language models improve the quality and efficiency of health policy surveillance?
desc: [Health affairs scholar] Legal epidemiology is a growing field wherein researchers examine the effects of health policies on health outcomes. Policy surveillance is a key part of the legal epidemiology process and leads to the creation of a legal dataset for econometric analyses. Policy surveillance includes conceptualizing the research scope, collecting legal data, and coding data to answer legal questions. Historically, policy surveillance has been slow and time-consuming, limiting timely information about the effects of health policies on health outcomes. Researchers are exploring the role of artificial intelligence using large language models (LLMs) to increase the efficiency and quality of the policy surveillance process. In this commentary, we describe potential uses of LLMs by researchers conducting policy surveillance as well as potential challenges that will need to be addressed before LLMs are widely used in the process. We also suggest areas for future research while emphasizing the need for development of guidelines for LLM use in policy surveillance.

title: Clinical Photography's Computational Blind Spot.
source: PubMed · The Australasian journal of dermatology
desc: [The Australasian journal of dermatology] The smartphone has become dermatology's primary clinical camera, yet the photo it saves is assembled by software rather than being a faithful unedited photograph: several frames are merged, grain is removed, and texture is altered before the image file exists, so no unedited original survives. This processing is hidden, inconsistent between shots, recorded only in undocumented vendor-specific form, and cannot be fully disabled in the camera app. Smartphone photographs still serve to locate a lesion and support a referral, but the processing pipeline is ill-suited and potentially misleading for serial monitoring, research, and training of artificial intelligence models. We propose a per-image record of capture and processing, practical measures clinicians can take now, and smartphone camera processing pipelines built for clinical fidelity rather than aesthetic ends.

title: Bilayer Na-MMT-Intercalated Guar Gum Triboelectric Nanogenerator With Graphite-Infused Electrodes for Machine Learning-Assisted Neck Posture Monitoring.
desc: [Small methods] Prolonged screen use has fostered cervical musculoskeletal disorders, indicating the need for non-invasive, comfortable, low-power posture monitoring system. In this work, we developed a sustainable self-powered triboelectric nanogenerator consisting a biodegradable guar gum-based biopolymer for energy harvesting and neck posture monitoring. The device employing a bilayer architecture, comprises a guar gum-bentonite triboelectric film coated with a guar gum-graphite conductive electrode, eliminating the need for a metallic electrode. The addition of Na-bentonite filler improves the dielectric and surface charge properties, producing a stable electrical output. As a flexible patch, the G-TENG measures unique biomechanical voltage signals representing neck flexion and slouching posture. The analysis of these electrical signals with machine learning algorithms enables the precise classification of neck angle and sitting postures. This current study presents a strategy for green, self-powered electronics that bridge personalized digital healthcare with sustainable biopolymers to mitigate global e-waste.

title: Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.
desc: [Molecular plant] Plant breeding is entering a multimodal era in which genomic, phenotypic, environmental, and multi-omics data are generated alongside a rapidly expanding scientific literature. Text-based large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models (Bio-FMs) offer complementary capabilities for organizing evidence, representing biological relationships, and learning from molecular data. Here, we review these technologies across knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and intelligent breeding design, and apply a systematic evidence audit to distinguish what each model family has directly demonstrated, where conclusions depend on adjacent or non-LLM evidence, and where key validation gaps remain. The audit shows that direct text-based LLM evidence is concentrated in retrieval, question answering, and evidence organization. Molecular prediction tasks, such as functional annotation and variant-effect prediction, rely mainly on Bio-FMs, whereas quantitative evidence for genomic prediction and G×E still comes largely from quantitative-genetic and deep-learning models. LLM-informed genomic prediction, parental selection, and breeding design therefore remain prospective. Moving them into practice will require reliable provenance, appropriate benchmarking, and validation matched to each output, from computational evaluation to experiments and field trials. LLM and Bio-FM outputs should support, rather than replace, scientific interpretation and breeder decision-making.

title: Steroid minimization in nephrotic syndrome relapses.
desc: [Pediatric nephrology (Berlin, Germany)] Corticosteroids remain the cornerstone of therapy for nephrotic syndrome (NS), yet cumulative exposure from repeated treatment courses during relapses contributes to substantial short- and long-term toxicity. Although several controlled trials have examined corticosteroid-sparing strategies, including reduced doses, shortened treatment durations, and single-dose regimens, robust evidence to define the optimal corticosteroid regimen for relapse management remains limited. Well-powered, high-quality randomized controlled trials are needed to establish standardized, evidence-based approaches to relapse treatment. This review summarizes current evidence on corticosteroid dosing strategies and proposes approaches to minimize corticosteroid exposure in children with relapsing NS. Future directions incorporating biomarkers, pharmacogenomics, artificial intelligence, and improved assessment of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis recovery may enable a more personalized approach to corticosteroid therapy in this population.

title: Algorithmic Bioethics: A Defense and Demonstration.
desc: [Bioethics] In this paper, we argue for the adoption of algorithmic bioethics, which uses algorithms, in the form of decision trees, to articulate, understand, apply, and evaluate bioethical arguments. Algorithms bring many benefits to the study of bioethics: they clearly, precisely, and transparently articulate the decision procedure and facts relevant to an ethical decision; furthermore, they can be used to systematically discover, map out, and compare different ethical decision procedures concerning a practical issue. We then also outline and tackle potential limitations of algorithmic bioethics, and explore future directions for using decision trees in bioethics. Throughout, we illustrate our points using a case study of ethical decision trees, created with the help of large language models, about conscientious objection in medicine.

title: Limitations of de novo peptide sequencing in resolving sequence ambiguity.
desc: [Nature methods] De novo peptide sequencing enables peptide identification from fragmentation spectra without relying on sequence databases. However, incomplete spectra create ambiguity, making unambiguous identification challenging. Recent deep learning advances have produced numerous de novo models that predict sequences and refine peptide-spectrum matches under such conditions. Yet, their relative strengths, weaknesses and ability to handle spectrum ambiguity remain unclear. Here we benchmark eight state-of-the-art models on three publicly available proteomics datasets, comparing performance using established metrics and quantifying inter-model agreement. We assess post-processing approaches, including iterative refinement, rescoring and reranking, for their ability to improve identification accuracy, and perform an error analysis to identify common mispredictions and their causes. Model performance varied, with considerable overlap of correct identifications. Post-processing yielded no or only modest improvements. Most sequencing errors were model-independent and driven by limited fragment ion coverage, a limitation also observed in database searches with large search spaces.

title: LTVAE: Hybrid LSTM-Transformer VAE Architecture for Molecular SMILES Representation.
desc: [Journal of computational chemistry] A hybrid LSTM-Transformer Variational Autoencoder (LTVAE) framework is introduced in this paper for learning compact and chemically meaningful latent representations from SMILES strings, providing a SMILES-to-latent-to-SMILES representation model trained on ZINC15 and evaluated on ZINC15 and an out-of-distribution dye dataset. In the proposed model, sequential and structural dependencies in molecular strings are encoded using a bidirectional LSTM, while a Transformer-based decoder is employed to reconstruct valid molecular structures in the evaluated settings. When trained on a curated ZINC15 dataset, the framework achieves reasonable reconstruction performance, with 98.58% token-level accuracy, 92.19% string-level accuracy, a 99.30% chemical validity ratio, and an average Levenshtein distance of 0.29 using a 64-dimensional latent space. Reconstruction under an out-of-distribution evaluation setting is evaluated on a structurally distinct dye dataset, where 95.56% token-level accuracy and 85.30% validity are achieved. The learned latent space preserves trends aligned with both general molecular descriptors and dye-relevant structural descriptors, particularly conjugation length and aromatic surface fraction, with Fsp 3 providing complementary information on molecular saturation. Controlled perturbations in the latent space suggest smooth and chemically consistent structural variations, illustrating the continuity and interpretability of the learned latent manifold.
